question: The International Space Station circles Earth roughly ______ times a day.
solution:
The correct answer is __**16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** orbits the Earth at an average altitude of approximately **408 kilometers (253 miles)**.
 
• It completes one orbit around the Earth in approximately **90 minutes**, traveling at a speed of around **28,000 kilometers per hour (17,500 miles per hour)**.
 
• Due to its orbital speed and duration, the ISS circles the Earth about **16 times a day**, providing astronauts the chance to witness 16 sunrises and sunsets daily.
 
• The specific orbital mechanics of the ISS ensure that it maintains a low Earth orbit, allowing it to remain in continuous motion around the Earth.
 
• This frequency of orbit facilitates various scientific experiments and observations, as the ISS provides multiple views of the Earth’s surface in a single day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of the ISS:**

 
 
• The ISS is a joint project involving **NASA** (United States), **Roscosmos** (Russia), **ESA** (European Space Agency), **JAXA** (Japan), and **CSA** (Canada).
 
• It serves as a unique microgravity laboratory, enabling scientists to conduct experiments in biology, physics, astronomy, and other fields that require the absence of gravity.
 
• The ISS has been continuously occupied since **November 2000**, making it one of the longest-running human spaceflight missions in history.
 
• The station is modular, with components such as living quarters, laboratories, and storage units assembled in orbit since its launch in **1998**.
 
• The ISS weighs approximately **420,000 kilograms (925,000 pounds)** and spans the size of a football field, making it the largest human-made structure in space.
 
 
 
• **Orbital Mechanics:**
 
 
• The ISS orbits in a **low Earth orbit (LEO)**, which ranges between **180 and 2,000 kilometers (111–1,243 miles)** above the Earth's surface.
 
• Its orbit is inclined at an angle of **51.6 degrees** to the equator, allowing it to cover most of the Earth's populated areas.
 
• The speed and altitude of the ISS are carefully maintained to counteract atmospheric drag and gravitational forces, ensuring it stays in orbit.
 
• Occasional adjustments, known as **reboosts**, are performed using onboard thrusters or visiting spacecraft to maintain its altitude.
 
 
 
• **Astronauts’ Perspective:**
 
 
• Due to the ISS’s frequent orbits, astronauts experience 16 sunrises and sunsets daily, providing a unique perspective on Earth’s atmosphere and weather patterns.
 
• The rapid orbital motion enables the station to pass over different continents multiple times in a single day, enhancing global observational capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Contribution:**
 
 
• The ISS enables groundbreaking research in areas like **medicine**, **climate change**, and **materials science**.
 
• It acts as a testing ground for technologies that will support future human exploration missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
